summary.en: Communal clashes continue in Jonglei, where an attack on Miny Island left dozens missing and a cattle keeper was injured by a wild animal in Aweil North, while a truck driver was killed on the Juba-Nimule road. The UN special envoy is urging President Kiir and other leaders to choose consensus over confrontation, and the African Union has voiced deep concerns about the renewed clashes. Uganda defended its military deployment in South Sudan and the US ambassador met with Kiir to discuss communal conflicts. A pastor received death threats in a refugee camp and a Juba Dal activist was hacked to death in Cumilla. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kommunale sammenstøt fortsetter i Jonglei, hvor et angrep på Miny-øya etterlot dusinvis savnet og en husdyrholder ble skadet av et vilt dyr i Aweil North, mens en lastebilsjåfør ble drept på Juba-Nimule-veien. FN-spesialutsendingen oppfordrer president Kiir og andre ledere til å velge konsensus fremfor konfrontasjon, og Den afrikanske union har uttrykt dyp bekymring over de fornyede sammenstøtene. Uganda forsvarte sin militære innsats i Sør-Sudan og den amerikanske ambassadøren møtte Kiir for å diskutere kommunale konflikter. En pastor mottok dødstrusler i en flyktningleir og en Juba Dal-aktivist ble hugget i hjel i Cumilla. To dødsfall knyttet til kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
